correctness.rationale: K_{3,n} spanning trees use n+2 edges, at least one from each of n right vertices, leaving precisely two surplus incidences. Either one right vertex has degree 3 or two distinct right vertices have degree 2 and different pairs of left vertices; all degree-2 pair choices with equal pairs are disconnected. For signed triples (a_i,b_i,c_i), s_i=a_i+b_i+c_i in +/-1,+/-3 is nonzero. Expanding prod(s_i)Phi(sum (a_ib_i,a_ic_i,b_ic_i)/s_i) gives precisely these tree cases; the diagonal identity Phi(v_i)=a_ib_ic_i/s_i follows from sign squares=1. Under uniformly random Walsh signs, E|s_i|=3/2, so tilting by |s_i|/12 gives eight vectors with weights 1/4 for two all-equal and 1/12 for six others; the exact norm is their absolute quadratic first moment times (3/2)^n. Symmetry gives mean zero and covariance diag 5/9, off -1/9. Bounded independent summands give uniform fourth moment for n^-1/2 sum, hence quadratic uniform integrability in the 3D CLT. In covariance eigenbasis Phi(Z)=(U0^2-U1^2-U2^2)/3 with iid standard Gaussians, and independent beta(1/2,1) ratio gives the exact integral int_0^1|2u^2-1|du=(2sqrt2-1)/3. Endpoint convolution ell1 and ellinfty norms equal the kernel absolute sum. All-n results are analytic, not inferred from finite checks.
